claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys can serve as low-activation structural materials for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Adding refractory elements with low activation cross-sections can optimize the composition of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The added refractory elements have low activation cross-sections.
Optimizing the elemental composition enhances irradiation resistance.
Optimizing the elemental composition reduces activation.
Enhanced irradiation resistance and reduced activation improve the performance of plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Enhanced irradiation resistance and reduced activation improve the durability of plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
The proposed refractory high-entropy alloys would perform better than traditional materials used in fusion reactors.
Suitability is bounded by high-temperature conditions and irradiation-resistance requirements.
The exact composition and proportions of refractory elements required for optimal performance are unknown.
